# RigorRun

> Permission and scope tests for AI agents, run before the agent ships. RigorRun
> sends an agent tickets that tempt it to act for the wrong customer or outside
> its job, then decides pass or fail by reading the real system afterwards — not
> the agent's transcript, and never with a model as the judge.

RigorRun is a local-first CLI, published on npm as `rigorrun`, MIT licensed, with
SLSA build provenance. It runs entirely on the user's machine: there is no account
and no hosted component.

## What is checked today

- The first pack is Stripe refunds (`npx rigorrun stripe twin`, then
  `npx rigorrun stripe init --twin --yes`): seven tickets, including a refund on
  another customer's payment, a disputed payment and an instruction inside the
  ticket. Each is decided from what Stripe holds afterwards.
- It was qualified before release against an independent oracle: 168 cells on a
  local Stripe twin and 168 on Stripe test mode, no false pass and no false fail;
  black-box mode 36 cells, none either.
- Every Stripe verdict is PARTIAL: it reads what each case created, not the
  whole account.

## Being built (not available yet)

- Being built: checks on what the agent read and what it sent, from its tool
  calls, the system's access log and marker strings planted in another
  customer's data (being built, not available yet).
- Being built next: a multi-tenant helpdesk pack, then the same checks on the
  user's own system.

## Key distinctions

- It is not an LLM evaluation harness. Evals grade what the agent said;
  RigorRun reads what happened in the system.
- It is not a runtime guard or policy engine. It checks, before release, that
  the permissions the agent should respect actually held.
- Every verdict carries a verification strength: AUTHORITATIVE, PARTIAL or
  OBSERVATIONAL.

## Honest limits

No external team has used RigorRun yet. There are no customers, no funding and no
revenue. The founder is looking for 3–5 design partners.
